unit.title: The tribunal's own architecture
unit.moc: files are the only state — the hub CLI — lanes & the family rule — routing — grounding — convergence — state layout — claim ledger & MoC

checkpoint.title: Checkpoint 3 — gate (the core one)
checkpoint.prompt: Describe the whole machinery — fanout → convergence → verify → record — and where the claim ledger and the MoC sit in it.

facts.text: Files are the only state; the session is disposable. A fresh session becomes the hub by reading THIS document + `ledger.md` — that pair is the entire bootstrap, and it kills the single-session dependency.

exercises.prompt: What is the tribunal's only state?
What does a fresh session need to read to become the hub?
options: a snapshot of the model weights

exercises.prompt: The clean-session bootstrap was proven on 2026-08-12 — a fresh shell with zero inherited env found `hub` and ran the whole loop from files alone.

facts.text: The `hub` CLI does `new`/`run`/`verdict`/`eval`/`gate`/`gate-backfill`/`winrate`/`playbook`/`cost`/`moc`/`status`/`log` — blind + parallel fanout, a self-rolled per-lane timeout watchdog (no GNU `timeout` on macOS), retry-once loop controller with keep-best, gate-enforced verdicts (`--force` = human override), and ledger-per-Quorum.

exercises.prompt: What does `hub run` do?
options: blind + parallel fanout of the brief to the lanes

exercises.prompt: The watchdog is:
options: a self-rolled per-lane timeout watchdog, no GNU timeout needed

exercises.prompt: What enforces a verdict in `hub`?
options: gate-enforced verdicts, with `--force` as the human override

facts.text: The lane inventory is live-tested: cc-fable (Claude, strongest) · cc-ds / oc-ds (DeepSeek flash) · cc-pro / oc-pro (DeepSeek reasoning) · oc-qw (local) · oc-or / oc-light (nemotron) · oc-nim (gpt-oss) · crush-glm. Family rule: count DeepSeek once — cc-ds, oc-ds, cc-pro, oc-pro share the DeepSeek family, pick ONE per sitting; nemotron max 2.

exercises.prompt: How many DeepSeek-family lanes may a sitting use?
The reason for the family rule is:
Match each lane family to its rule.

facts.text: Default panel = 2 lanes; 4 only for high stakes. Each problem class has a lane default: factcheck → cheap independent votes with cc-fable only to break ties; code debug → oc-ds + oc-qw; deep reasoning → oc-pro/cc-pro + oc-qw; secrets/client data → oc-qw ONLY (never leaves the machine).

exercises.prompt: The default panel is ___ lanes.
4 lanes are used only for:
For secrets/client data, the only lane is:

facts.text: `sb` answers “true in MY repos”; fresh docs answer “true TODAY”; lanes answer “generally true.” Every verdict cites at least one of the first two. Refuse or downgrade to opinion when there is no `sb` hit and no fetchable doc, or the question needs data the owner didn't provide.

exercises.prompt: Every verdict must cite at least one of:
options: an `sb` chunk or a fresh doc

exercises.prompt: When there is no `sb` hit and no fetchable doc, the tribunal should:
Which of these is a GROUNDING violation?
exercises.scenario: A lane writes a verdict citing only another lane's opinion, with no `sb` chunk and no fresh doc.

facts.text: Facts decompose into atomic claims; accept ONLY if the claim survives a grounding source. Agreement without a source = “probable, unverified” — label it. Majority alone is convergence theater: same-family models hallucinate the same “fact” together — 3 of 4 lanes explicitly reject majority voting. Verifier: a FRESH lane armed with the evidence arbitrates; rotate it so Claude doesn't silently become ground truth.

exercises.prompt: Majority agreement WITHOUT a source is labeled:
Why is majority alone “convergence theater”?
options: same-family models hallucinate the same “fact” together

exercises.prompt: The verifier role should be:
options: a fresh lane armed with the evidence, rotated

facts.text: Per problem in `sidequests/<slug>/`: `intake.md` (problem + success criteria), `lanes/` (raw outputs, one file per lane), `verdict.md` (converged answer + dissents + citations). Plus ONE line in a global `ledger.md` — date, class, lanes used, winner, cost.

exercises.prompt: The per-sitting layout: sidequests/<slug>/ = intake.md, ___, and verdict.md; plus one line in the global ___.
The ledger line records:
options: date, class, lanes used, winner, cost

exercises.prompt: `verdict.md` contains:

facts.text: The claim-ledger schema (borrowed from claude-obsidian): claim_id, sitting, class, claim, source, support, contradiction, confidence (probable|verified|contested), review_state (open|accepted|rejected|stale), added, reviewed. The ledger is generated by `hub eval`, never hand-maintained.
The MoC is a single Mermaid map of contents — nodes = sittings, edges = frontmatter links (`relates:`/`supersedes:`/`depends_on:`) — regenerated by `hub moc`.

exercises.prompt: Which of these is a claim-ledger confidence value?
A claim is `accepted` only after:
The MoC is:
options: a Mermaid map of contents, nodes = sittings
